endpoints.name: Abuse Report
endpoints.description: One abuse report by id, with the reporter and the object reported. Community moderation, and the record behind removed content.

endpoints.name: Acclaims
endpoints.description: The acclaim awarded within the community. Recognition at the community level.

endpoints.name: Action
endpoints.description: One action by id.

endpoints.name: Actions
endpoints.description: The actionable items assigned to the calling user -- approvals, mentions, tasks awaiting response. The personal work queue.

endpoints.name: Actions Counts
endpoints.description: How many actions are outstanding, by type. The badge counts, without fetching the items.

endpoints.name: Activities
endpoints.description: The community activity stream -- every action taken, with the actor, the verb, the object acted on and the timestamp. THE BEHAVIOURAL RECORD, as opposed to the content tables which hold what exists: who read, liked, commented, followed and created, and when. Filterable by time and by activity type. Note streams have a retention window, so this is not a permanent history.

endpoints.name: Activities Count
endpoints.description: How many activities match given filters, without returning them. The cheap size check.

endpoints.name: Frequent Content
endpoints.description: The content the calling user interacts with most. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Frequent People
endpoints.description: The people the calling user interacts with most. Personalised -- and one of the few endpoints that measures working relationships rather than declared ones.

endpoints.name: Frequent Places
endpoints.description: The places the calling user visits most. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Add On
endpoints.description: One add-on by id, with its status. Add-ons provide tiles, external streams and app content, so this explains community features and data that Jive itself did not produce.

endpoints.name: Plugin
endpoints.description: One plugin by id.

endpoints.name: Plugins
endpoints.description: The plugins installed on the instance. Administrative inventory.

endpoints.name: Profile Field
endpoints.description: One profile field by id.

endpoints.name: Profile Field Name
endpoints.description: One profile field by name.

endpoints.name: Profile Fields
endpoints.description: The profile fields configured community-wide, with their types and whether each is searchable. THE DECODER for the profile field values on a person, and the statement of what the organisation records about people.

endpoints.name: Properties
endpoints.description: The system properties of the instance. Administrative configuration, and worth checking when a feature-dependent endpoint returns nothing.

endpoints.name: Property
endpoints.description: One system property by name.

endpoints.name: Announcement
endpoints.description: One announcement by id, with its body and the place it applies to.

endpoints.name: System Announcements
endpoints.description: The community-wide announcements currently active. Administrative communication rather than user content.

endpoints.name: Attachment
endpoints.description: One attachment by id.

endpoints.name: Attachments
endpoints.description: The attachments on one object. Requires the object id. Metadata; binaries are separate.

endpoints.name: Event Calendar
endpoints.description: The calendar of events in the community, with their dates and places. Events are content with a schedule, so they appear in the content tables too -- this is the time-ordered view.

endpoints.name: Check Points
endpoints.description: The checkpoints of one video, marking positions viewers reached. Requires the video id. Video engagement depth, as opposed to view counts.

endpoints.name: Collaboration
endpoints.description: One collaboration session by id -- Jive's real-time co-editing record.

endpoints.name: Collaboration by External ID
endpoints.description: One collaboration by the external system's identifier.

endpoints.name: Interaction
endpoints.description: One interaction by id.

endpoints.name: Interaction Optionally With Context
endpoints.description: One interaction with its surrounding context, where available.

endpoints.name: Interactions
endpoints.description: The interactions within collaborations -- the individual actions taken in a session. Fine-grained collaboration telemetry.

endpoints.name: Participants
endpoints.description: Who took part in one collaboration. Requires the collaboration id.

endpoints.name: Abuse Reports for Comment
endpoints.description: The abuse reports raised against one comment. Requires the comment id.

endpoints.name: Comment
endpoints.description: One comment by id, with its body and author.

endpoints.name: Comment Likes
endpoints.description: Who liked one comment. Requires the comment id.

endpoints.name: Comment Comments
endpoints.description: The replies to one comment. Requires the comment id. Comments nest, so a full thread means walking this.

endpoints.name: Editable Comment
endpoints.description: Whether the calling user may edit one comment. A permission check.

endpoints.name: Comment Marked Helpful
endpoints.description: Whether one comment is marked helpful, and by whom. Requires the comment id. IN A SUPPORT COMMUNITY THIS IS THE QUALITY SIGNAL -- a helpful mark says an answer worked, which no like count conveys.

endpoints.name: Comment Marked Unhelpful
endpoints.description: Whether one comment is marked unhelpful. The negative signal, and worth reading alongside the positive rather than instead of it.

endpoints.name: Comment Outcome Types
endpoints.description: The outcome types applicable to one comment. Requires the comment id.

endpoints.name: Abuse Reports for Content
endpoints.description: The abuse reports raised against one content object. Requires the content id. Moderation, and the explanation for content that disappeared.

endpoints.name: Child Outcome Types
endpoints.description: The outcome types applicable to the children of one content object. Requires the content id.

endpoints.name: Content Comments
endpoints.description: The comments on one content object. Requires the content id. Where discussion beneath a document or blog post lives.

endpoints.name: Content Data
endpoints.description: One content object by id, with its full body and metadata. Requires the content id.

endpoints.name: Content Followers
endpoints.description: Who follows one content object. Requires the content id. Following is Jive's subscription mechanism, so this is the audience that gets notified about a document.

endpoints.name: Content Following In
endpoints.description: The streams one content object is being followed in. Requires the content id.

endpoints.name: Content Likes
endpoints.description: Who liked one content object. Requires the content id. The content record carries a like count; this is who they were.

endpoints.name: Contents
endpoints.description: ALL CONTENT IN THE COMMUNITY IN ONE TABLE -- documents, discussions, blog posts, polls, ideas, files, videos and status updates are every one of them 'content', told apart by a TYPE field. This polymorphism is the defining fact of the Jive API and it repeats for places and activities: one endpoint, many shapes, and a type discriminator deciding which fields are even present. So any question about a particular kind of content is a filter on type, and a count taken without one counts everything the community has ever produced. TWO OTHER THINGS APPLY THROUGHOUT. The FILTER parameter takes Jive's own syntax -- type(document), place(...), search(...), tag(...) -- and is the only real query mechanism. And the FIELDS parameter decides which fields come back: Jive returns a default subset, so most of a content object is absent unless named.

endpoints.name: Editable Content
endpoints.description: The content the calling user may edit. A permission view, scoped to the caller.

endpoints.name: Featured Content
endpoints.description: The content editorially marked as featured. A human choice rather than a computed one.

endpoints.name: My Entitlements
endpoints.description: The permissions the calling user holds on one content object. Requires the content id. Why the caller can or cannot act on it.

endpoints.name: Content Outcomes
endpoints.description: The outcomes marked on one content object -- resolved, decision, action item, success and the rest. Requires the content id. OUTCOMES ARE HOW JIVE RECORDS THAT SOMETHING WAS SETTLED: a discussion with an answer is distinguished from one without only by an outcome, so question-resolution rates depend entirely on this table.

endpoints.name: Content Outcome Types
endpoints.description: The outcome types that may be applied to one content object. Requires the content id. Which outcomes are permitted depends on the content type, so this is the per-object vocabulary.

endpoints.name: Popular Content
endpoints.description: The content ranked by engagement over a period. Jive's own popularity calculation rather than a raw count.

endpoints.name: Preview Image
endpoints.description: The preview image of one content object. Requires the content id. Presentation.

endpoints.name: Recent Content
endpoints.description: The content most recently created or modified across the community. The incremental view, and the practical entry point when the question is about what changed.

endpoints.name: Recommended Content
endpoints.description: Content Jive recommends to the calling user. Personalised, so it describes the caller rather than the community.

endpoints.name: Trending Content
endpoints.description: The content gaining engagement fastest right now. Distinct from popular: trending is about acceleration, popular about volume, and a piece of content can be one without the other.

endpoints.name: User Entitlements
endpoints.description: The permissions a named user holds on one content object. Requires the content id.

endpoints.name: Deleted Contents
endpoints.description: The content deleted since a given time. THE ONLY WAY A SYNCHRONISED COPY LEARNS THAT CONTENT HAS GONE -- deletions leave no trace in the content tables, so a downstream store diverges silently without this.

endpoints.name: Deleted Object
endpoints.description: One deleted object's record, by id.

endpoints.name: Deleted People
endpoints.description: The people deleted since a given time.

endpoints.name: Deleted Places
endpoints.description: The places deleted since a given time.

endpoints.name: Direct Message Comments
endpoints.description: The replies within one direct message thread. Requires the message id.

endpoints.name: Direct Message Images
endpoints.description: The images within one direct message. Requires the message id.

endpoints.name: Direct Message
endpoints.description: One direct message by id. Private messages between users, invisible in the content and activity tables, which is why community-wide engagement figures understate real communication.

endpoints.name: Event Type
endpoints.description: One event type by id.

endpoints.name: Event Types
endpoints.description: The event types configured. The decoder for an event's type.

endpoints.name: External Stream Definition
endpoints.description: One external stream definition by id.

endpoints.name: External Stream Definition I18n Resource
endpoints.description: The translated strings of one external stream definition.

endpoints.name: External Stream Definitions
endpoints.description: The external stream types add-ons provide.

endpoints.name: Prototype
endpoints.description: A prototype external stream object. Scaffolding.

endpoints.name: External Stream Tile Category
endpoints.description: The tile category associated with an external stream definition.

endpoints.name: Specified External Stream Instance
endpoints.description: One external stream instance by id.

endpoints.name: Instance by External ID
endpoints.description: One external stream instance by the external system's identifier.

endpoints.name: External Stream Instances
endpoints.description: The external stream instances configured -- integrations pushing activity from other systems into Jive streams. WHERE ACTIVITY FROM OUTSIDE JIVE ENTERS: the activity tables include these, so an activity count spans systems, and this is what says which.

endpoints.name: External Stream Private Properties
endpoints.description: The private configuration of one external stream instance.

endpoints.name: Content Votes
endpoints.description: The votes cast on one poll or idea. Requires the content id. THE OUTCOME OF A POLL OR IDEA lives here rather than on the content itself, so a result is only readable through this.

endpoints.name: Content Images
endpoints.description: The images embedded in one content object. Requires the content id.

endpoints.name: Image
endpoints.description: One image by id.

endpoints.name: Activity Inbox
endpoints.description: The calling user's inbox stream -- everything they are meant to see. Scoped to the caller, so it describes one person's attention rather than the community.

endpoints.name: Counts
endpoints.description: The unread counts of the calling user's inbox.

endpoints.name: Invite
endpoints.description: One invitation by id. Pending membership, which no member list shows.

endpoints.name: Place Invites
endpoints.description: The invitations to join one place. Requires the place id. Pending membership, which the member list does not show.

endpoints.name: All Invites
endpoints.description: Every outstanding invitation. The onboarding backlog.

endpoints.name: Member
endpoints.description: One membership record by id, with the person and group and the role held.

endpoints.name: Members by Group
endpoints.description: The members of one security group. Requires the group id.

endpoints.name: Members by Person
endpoints.description: The groups one person belongs to. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Mention
endpoints.description: One mention by id -- a reference to a person inside content. Mentions are how attention is directed in Jive, so they are a better signal of who is being pulled into work than follower counts.

endpoints.name: Content Replies
endpoints.description: The replies to one message. Requires the message id. Discussions are threaded through messages rather than comments, which is why both exist.

endpoints.name: Editable Message
endpoints.description: Whether the calling user may edit one message. A permission check.

endpoints.name: Message Marked Helpful
endpoints.description: Whether one message is marked helpful, and by whom. Requires the message id.

endpoints.name: Message Marked Unhelpful
endpoints.description: Whether one message is marked unhelpful. Requires the message id.

endpoints.name: Message
endpoints.description: One message by id -- a reply within a discussion thread. Discussions are built from messages, not comments, which is the distinction to keep straight when counting participation.

endpoints.name: Message Likes
endpoints.description: Who liked one message. Requires the message id.

endpoints.name: Message Outcomes
endpoints.description: The outcomes marked on one message. Requires the message id. A message marked as the correct answer is how a question is resolved, so this is the resolution record for discussions.

endpoints.name: Message Replies
endpoints.description: The replies to one message. Requires the message id. How a discussion thread branches.

endpoints.name: Available Locale Metadata
endpoints.description: The locales the instance could offer.

endpoints.name: Supported Locale Metadata
endpoints.description: The locales the instance actually supports. Content and profile fields are localised, so this bounds what a multilingual query can ask for.

endpoints.name: All Object Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata of every object type. The whole schema in one call.

endpoints.name: Field Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata of one field -- its type, constraints and whether it is filterable.

endpoints.name: Field Metadata Values
endpoints.description: The permitted values of one field. The decoder for that field's codes.

endpoints.name: Object Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata of one object type -- its fields, their types and their constraints. Requires the type name.

endpoints.name: Object Metadata Values
endpoints.description: The permitted values of one object type's enumerated fields. The decoder for coded values.

endpoints.name: Object Types
endpoints.description: The object types the API exposes. THE ROOT OF JIVE'S METADATA MODEL, which is unusually complete: the platform describes its own schema, so what a field means and which values it accepts are answerable from the API rather than from documentation.

endpoints.name: All Property Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata of every system property.

endpoints.name: Property Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata of one system property.

endpoints.name: All Public Property Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata of the publicly readable properties. The subset available without administrative rights.

endpoints.name: Public Property Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata of one public property.

endpoints.name: Field Resource Metadata
endpoints.description: The API resources associated with one field.

endpoints.name: Object Resource Metadata
endpoints.description: The API resources available on one object type. What can be done with it.

endpoints.name: Object Type Mappings
endpoints.description: How object type names map to their identifiers. The translation between the names used in filters and those in responses.

endpoints.name: All Time Zone Metadata
endpoints.description: Every time zone the instance recognises. Relevant because activity timestamps are rendered per user.

endpoints.name: Time Zone Metadata
endpoints.description: One time zone's metadata.

endpoints.name: Moderation Counts
endpoints.description: How many items await moderation, by type. The backlog size.

endpoints.name: Moderation
endpoints.description: The moderation queue -- content awaiting approval. Content in moderation is NOT visible in the ordinary content listings, so a publishing-volume figure omits it until it is approved.

endpoints.name: Pending Moderation
endpoints.description: The items awaiting moderation for the calling user, as a moderator.

endpoints.name: Embed
endpoints.description: The oEmbed representation of a URL. A rendering helper rather than data.

endpoints.name: History
endpoints.description: The history of outcomes on one object. Requires the object id. An outcome can be changed or removed, so this is the record of how a resolution state evolved.

endpoints.name: Outcome
endpoints.description: One outcome by id, with the object it was applied to and by whom.

endpoints.name: Outcomes
endpoints.description: The outcomes recorded across the community -- resolved, decision, action item, success, helpful. OUTCOMES ARE HOW JIVE RECORDS THAT SOMETHING WAS SETTLED, so resolution rates, decision counts and unanswered-question analysis all reduce to this table.

endpoints.name: Page
endpoints.description: One page by id, with its tiles.

endpoints.name: Prototype Page
endpoints.description: A blank page object, for building a new one. Scaffolding rather than data.

endpoints.name: Activity Person
endpoints.description: The activity stream of one person. Requires the person id. What someone actually did, as opposed to what they are.

endpoints.name: All People
endpoints.description: Every person in the community, paged. The complete roster, as opposed to the filtered listing.

endpoints.name: Blog
endpoints.description: One person's blog. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Colleagues
endpoints.description: The colleagues of one person. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Common Bidirectional Related People
endpoints.description: The people two users have in common, following each other. THE SOCIAL GRAPH INTERSECTION -- who connects two people, which no directory can answer.

endpoints.name: Featured Content for Person
endpoints.description: The content featured for one person. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Filterable Fields
endpoints.description: The person fields that may be filtered on. Narrower than the supported set, and the limit on what a people query can ask.

endpoints.name: Followers
endpoints.description: Who follows one person. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Following
endpoints.description: Who one person follows. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Following In
endpoints.description: The streams one person is followed in. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Following Person
endpoints.description: Whether one person follows another. A relationship check.

endpoints.name: Manager
endpoints.description: One person's manager. Requires the person id. The organisational hierarchy, where Jive is fed from a directory.

endpoints.name: Metadata
endpoints.description: The metadata describing the person object. The schema behind a person record.

endpoints.name: News
endpoints.description: The news stream of one person. Requires the person id. What Jive presents to them, not what they produced.

endpoints.name: Pages
endpoints.description: The custom pages built in the community. Layout containers assembled from tiles.

endpoints.name: Pages Prototype
endpoints.description: A prototype page object for one person, for building a new page.

endpoints.name: Pending Expertise Tags
endpoints.description: The expertise endorsements awaiting one person's acceptance. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: People
endpoints.description: The users of the community, with name, email, title, location, the profile fields, and their follower and content counts. Filterable and field-selectable like everything else here.

endpoints.name: Person by ID
endpoints.description: One person by id.

endpoints.name: Person by Email
endpoints.description: One person by email address. The lookup when the id is unknown.

endpoints.name: Person by External Identity
endpoints.description: One person by an identity from an external system. THE BRIDGE from a corporate directory or single-sign-on identifier to a Jive user, which no other endpoint provides.

endpoints.name: Person by Username
endpoints.description: One person by username.

endpoints.name: Private Properties for Person
endpoints.description: The private properties stored against one person. Requires the person id. Application storage rather than profile data.

endpoints.name: Profile Field Privacy
endpoints.description: The privacy setting of one profile field for a person. WHY A FIELD IS BLANK: a hidden field returns nothing, which looks identical to an unfilled one.

endpoints.name: Profile Fields Privacy
endpoints.description: The privacy settings of all profile fields for a person.

endpoints.name: Profile Image
endpoints.description: One person's profile image.

endpoints.name: Profile Images
endpoints.description: All profile images of one person.

endpoints.name: Recognition
endpoints.description: The recognition badges awarded to one person. Requires the person id. Jive's peer-recognition record.

endpoints.name: Recommended People
endpoints.description: People recommended to the calling user. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Report
endpoints.description: One direct report of a person.

endpoints.name: Reports
endpoints.description: The direct reports of one person. Requires the person id. Together with Manager this reconstructs the org chart.

endpoints.name: Person Resources
endpoints.description: The API resources available for one person. A discovery aid rather than data.

endpoints.name: Person Roles
endpoints.description: The roles one person holds. Requires the person id. Roles decide capability, so this is why two users can do different things.

endpoints.name: Security Groups for Person
endpoints.description: The security groups one person belongs to. Requires the person id. Group membership is how most access is granted, so this is the practical answer to what someone can reach.

endpoints.name: Social Users
endpoints.description: The external social accounts linked to one person. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Streams
endpoints.description: The custom streams defined -- the curated feeds users assemble from places, people and content they follow. A stream's ASSOCIATIONS state what its owner considered worth watching, which is a more honest signal of interest than following counts.

endpoints.name: Supported Fields
endpoints.description: The person fields the API supports returning. The vocabulary for the fields parameter.

endpoints.name: Tags on User
endpoints.description: The tags applied to one person. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Tasks
endpoints.description: The tasks assigned to one person. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Terms And Conditions
endpoints.description: The terms and conditions record for one person -- whether they accepted and when. Compliance evidence.

endpoints.name: Top Expertise
endpoints.description: The expertise tags one person is most endorsed for. Requires the person id.

endpoints.name: Trending Content for Person
endpoints.description: The content trending for one person. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Trending People
endpoints.description: The people gaining followers or engagement fastest.

endpoints.name: Trending Places for Person
endpoints.description: The places trending for one person. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Users by Expertise
endpoints.description: People holding a given expertise tag. EXPERTISE IS JIVE'S SKILLS MODEL, endorsed by colleagues rather than self-declared, so this is a socially validated answer to who knows about something.

endpoints.name: Who Endorsed
endpoints.description: Who endorsed one person for a given expertise. Requires the person id and tag. The evidence behind an expertise claim.

endpoints.name: Place Activity
endpoints.description: The activity stream of one place. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Place Applied Entitlements
endpoints.description: The entitlements actually in force on one place, after inheritance. Requires the place id. The resolved answer, as opposed to the configuration.

endpoints.name: Place Content
endpoints.description: The content inside one place. Requires the place id. The per-container view, and the usual route from an organisational unit to what it produced.

endpoints.name: Place Featured Content
endpoints.description: The content editorially featured in one place. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Place
endpoints.description: One place by id, with its settings and counts.

endpoints.name: Place Announcements
endpoints.description: The announcements posted in one place. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Place Avatar
endpoints.description: The avatar image of one place. Presentation.

endpoints.name: Place Categories
endpoints.description: The categories defined within one place. Requires the place id. A place's own content taxonomy, which is local rather than community-wide.

endpoints.name: Place Category
endpoints.description: One place category by id.

endpoints.name: Place Followers
endpoints.description: Who follows one place. Requires the place id. The audience a place's content reaches.

endpoints.name: Place Following In
endpoints.description: The streams one place is being followed in. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Place Permissions
endpoints.description: The permissions configured on one place. Requires the place id. Who may see and post, which is why two users see different content lists.

endpoints.name: Place Places
endpoints.description: The child places of one place. Requires the place id. Places nest, so a full tree means walking this repeatedly.

endpoints.name: Places
endpoints.description: THE CONTAINERS CONTENT LIVES IN -- spaces, groups and projects, again polymorphic and told apart by a type field. A space is the permanent organisational structure, a group is a self-forming community, a project is time-bounded work, and they behave differently enough that mixing them in one count is rarely meaningful. Same filter and fields rules as content.

endpoints.name: Place Settings
endpoints.description: The settings of one place. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Place Statics
endpoints.description: The static resources attached to one place. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Place Suggested Places
endpoints.description: Places Jive suggests as related to one place. Requires the place id. Derived rather than curated.

endpoints.name: Place Tasks
endpoints.description: The tasks within one place. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Recommended Places
endpoints.description: Places recommended to the calling user. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Root Space
endpoints.description: The top-level space of the community. The root of the place hierarchy, and the starting point for walking it.

endpoints.name: Suggested Places
endpoints.description: Places suggested to the calling user. Personalised.

endpoints.name: Trending Places
endpoints.description: The places gaining activity fastest. The community-wide view of where attention is moving.

endpoints.name: Place Template Categories
endpoints.description: The categories place templates are grouped into.

endpoints.name: Place Template Category
endpoints.description: One place template category by id.

endpoints.name: Place Template
endpoints.description: One place template by id.

endpoints.name: Place Templates
endpoints.description: The templates new places are created from. What the organisation considers a standard kind of space or group.

endpoints.name: Place Topic
endpoints.description: One place topic by id.

endpoints.name: Place Topics
endpoints.description: The topics of one place. Requires the place id.

endpoints.name: Publication
endpoints.description: One publication by id, with its sections.

endpoints.name: Publications
endpoints.description: The publications defined -- Jive's curated content collections, distributed on a schedule. Editorial rather than organic content.

endpoints.name: Subscriber Users
endpoints.description: Who subscribes to one publication. Requires the publication id. The reach of a curated channel.

endpoints.name: Have Same Questions
endpoints.description: The people who indicated they have the same question. Requires the content id. Demand for an answer, which the view count cannot express.

endpoints.name: RSVP Invitees
endpoints.description: Who was invited to one event, regardless of response. The denominator for any attendance figure.

endpoints.name: RSVP Maybe Attendees
endpoints.description: Who responded tentatively to one event.

endpoints.name: RSVP No Attendees
endpoints.description: Who declined one event.

endpoints.name: RSVP Events
endpoints.description: The events the calling user has been invited to.

endpoints.name: RSVP Yes Attendees
endpoints.description: Who accepted one event. Requires the event id. ATTENDANCE INTENT IS SPLIT ACROSS FOUR ENDPOINTS -- yes, no, maybe and invited -- so a response rate needs all of them, and the invited list is the denominator.

endpoints.name: Search Contents
endpoints.description: Content matching a search query. Jive's search takes its own filter syntax, and searching is usually faster than filtering the content listing when the question is about words rather than structure.

endpoints.name: Search People
endpoints.description: People matching a search term across name, title and profile fields.

endpoints.name: Search Places
endpoints.description: Places matching a search query.

endpoints.name: Search Tags
endpoints.description: Tags matching a search query. Useful for discovering the community's own vocabulary before filtering by tag.

endpoints.name: Section Avatar
endpoints.description: The avatar image of one section.

endpoints.name: Section
endpoints.description: One section by id.

endpoints.name: Sections
endpoints.description: The sections of a publication or support centre. The structural level below a publication.

endpoints.name: Group Administrators
endpoints.description: The administrators of one security group. Requires the group id.

endpoints.name: Group Member
endpoints.description: One member of a security group.

endpoints.name: Group Members
endpoints.description: The members of one security group. Requires the group id.

endpoints.name: Security Group by Name
endpoints.description: One security group by name.

endpoints.name: Security Groups
endpoints.description: The security groups defined -- the units access is granted to. Together with place permissions this is how visibility is actually determined, and why two users see different content.

endpoints.name: Share
endpoints.description: One share by id -- content passed to a person or place with a note. The internal amplification record.

endpoints.name: Slide
endpoints.description: One slide by id.

endpoints.name: Slides
endpoints.description: The slides of one presentation object. Requires the content id.

endpoints.name: Banner
endpoints.description: The support centre banner configuration. Presentation.

endpoints.name: Channels
endpoints.description: The support channels configured. How customers may reach support, which no ticket table states.

endpoints.name: Support Center Section
endpoints.description: One support centre section by id.

endpoints.name: Support Center Sections
endpoints.description: The sections within the support centre.

endpoints.name: Support Center Categories
endpoints.description: The categories of the support centre -- Jive's customer-facing help structure.

endpoints.name: Stage
endpoints.description: One stage by id.

endpoints.name: Stages
endpoints.description: The stages an idea moves through -- Jive's idea lifecycle. WHERE IDEAS SIT IN THE PROCESS, which the idea content object records only as a current value.

endpoints.name: Static
endpoints.description: One static resource by id.

endpoints.name: Statics
endpoints.description: The static resources uploaded to the community.

endpoints.name: Stream Comments
endpoints.description: The comments on one stream entry. Requires the entry id.

endpoints.name: Stream Likes
endpoints.description: The likes on one stream entry. Requires the entry id.

endpoints.name: Stream Activity
endpoints.description: The activity within one stream. Requires the stream id.

endpoints.name: Stream Activity Count
endpoints.description: How much activity one stream carries. The size check.

endpoints.name: Stream Association
endpoints.description: One stream association by id.

endpoints.name: Stream Associations
endpoints.description: What one stream is subscribed to. Requires the stream id. The stream's actual definition.

endpoints.name: Connections Activity
endpoints.description: The activity of the people the calling user is connected to. The social feed.

endpoints.name: Stream
endpoints.description: One stream by id.

endpoints.name: Tag
endpoints.description: One tag by name, with its usage. Tags are the community's free-form taxonomy, unconstrained and often near-duplicated.

endpoints.name: Tile Definition
endpoints.description: One tile definition -- the type of tile an add-on provides, as opposed to an instance of it.

endpoints.name: Tile Definition I18n Resource
endpoints.description: The translated strings of one tile definition.

endpoints.name: Tile Definition Instances
endpoints.description: The instances created from one tile definition. Requires the definition id. How widely an add-on's tile is actually used.

endpoints.name: Tile Definition Prototype
endpoints.description: A prototype tile object for a definition. Scaffolding.

endpoints.name: Tile Definition Categories
endpoints.description: The categories tile definitions are grouped into.

endpoints.name: Tile Definition Category
endpoints.description: One tile definition category by id.

endpoints.name: Tile Instance
endpoints.description: One tile instance by id.

endpoints.name: Tile Instance by External ID
endpoints.description: One tile instance by the external system's identifier. The bridge from an integration's own id to Jive's.

endpoints.name: Tile Instance Data
endpoints.description: THE DATA A TILE IS DISPLAYING. Requires the tile id. Where an integration has pushed content into Jive, this is the only place that content is readable -- it lives in the tile rather than in any content table.

endpoints.name: Tile Instances
endpoints.description: The tile instances across the community.

endpoints.name: Tile Private Properties
endpoints.description: The private configuration of one tile instance. Application storage.

endpoints.name: Tile Categories
endpoints.description: The categories tiles are grouped into.

endpoints.name: Tile Category
endpoints.description: One tile category by id.

endpoints.name: URL Comments
endpoints.description: The comments on one external URL object. Requires the URL id.

endpoints.name: Content External URLs
endpoints.description: The external links referenced by one content object. Requires the content id.

endpoints.name: External URL
endpoints.description: One external URL object by id. Jive tracks links shared into the community as objects, so this is how external references become countable.

endpoints.name: Version
endpoints.description: One version of one content object.

endpoints.name: Versions
endpoints.description: The version history of one content object. Requires the content id. Jive versions documents, so this is the only record of what a document said before it was edited -- and who changed it.

endpoints.name: Download Options
endpoints.description: The download formats available for one video. Requires the video id.

endpoints.name: Vitals
endpoints.description: The vital statistics of one object -- view, like, comment and follower counts in one call. Requires the object id. THE CHEAP ENGAGEMENT SUMMARY: it avoids fetching the likes, comments and followers separately when only the totals are wanted.

endpoints.name: Votes
endpoints.description: The votes cast on one poll. Requires the poll id. The result of a poll, which the poll object does not carry.
